A hairy marine worm that lives under beach sand. Live bait for ocean fishing.
A moth in the third stage of its development into an adult. Live bait for freshwater fishing.
A small insect covered in a grey protective carapace. Is known to curl up in a ball when agitated. Live bait for ocean fishing.
A ball of crayfish and rye flour paste. Processed bait for freshwater fishing.
A ball of goby and rye flour paste. Processed bait for ocean fishing.
A common earthworm that earns its name from the blood red tint of its body. Live bait for freshwater fishing.
The thin tail of a rat, often carried by young Lalafellin boys as a good-luck charm. Bait for ocean fishing.
A tightly knitted wicker basket filled with a swarm of biting midges. Live bait for freshwater fishing.
A ball of crabmeat and rye flour paste. Processed bait for ocean fishing.
If allowed to pupate, this bright-yellow larva will transform into a hideous moth which can devour an entire tunic in a single turn of the sun. Live bait for freshwater fishing.
A ball of dark bass and sunset flour paste. Processed bait for freshwater fishing.
Also colorfully known as a “fisherman's member,” the stench of this sea-dwelling creature when sliced up is perfect for attracting hungry fish. Live bait for ocean fishing.
A tightly knitted wicker basket filled with a swarm of angry syrphids. Live bait for freshwater fishing.
A ball of Indigo herring and sunset flour paste. Processed bait for ocean fishing.
The honeyfly will lay its eggs in beehives where, upon hatching, the larvae will feed on honey until pupation. Live bait for freshwater fishing.

A spineless creature which hides patiently under the desert─ofttimes for several moons─until a larger beast passes nearby. The leech will then attach itself to the new host's leg and proceed to drink deep of the beast's blood until its belly is full, after which it releases itself back to the desert to wait for its next victim. Live bait for dunefishing.
This longhorn beetle larva can most commonly be found burrowed deep into the trunks of fallen logs. Live bait for freshwater fishing.
When night falls, thousands of these tiny scalekin can be seen scampering about the Sagolii Desert in search of the beetles on which they dine. Live bait for dunefishing.

It is not known why one end of these vilekin shines bright like a candle. It is, however, known that the light emitted by these creatures makes them a perfect target for hungry fish. Live bait for freshwater and ocean fishing.
When threatened, this tiny desert crustacean will curl itself into a ball which, to the untrained eye, will appear no more than a simple pebble. Live bait for dunefishing.
Unlike other vilekin larvae, the hoverworm is not confined to life on the ground. Filling its belly with air allows it to freely ride the thermals over the Sea of Clouds. Live bait for skyfishing.
Microscopic shrimp which inhabit the colder sea currents hailing from the northern seas. Live bait for ocean fishing.
The fact they are extremely difficult to harvest from their underwater homes makes fishing with caddisfly larvae an option for only the most well-to-do anglers. Live bait for freshwater fishing.
Atypical of common caterpillars, this sand-dwelling species is covered in a rock-like outer skin which serves to prevent the loss of moisture to the hot desert sun. Live bait for dunefishing.

With wings too underdeveloped for flying, this beetle has adopted another method of locomotion about the Sea of Clouds─a second bladder it fills with a noxious lighter-than-air gas. This foul stench is known to attract larger, hungrier creatures. Live bait for skyfishing.
A freshwater fishing lure made from a chocobo feather. The faint aroma of stable hay brings back memories of a simpler time.
A light plug lure made to resemble a minnow. Especially effective when used to land fish swimming close to the water's surface.
A polished brass lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting fish. Especially effective in lakes.
A small metal cage packed with a pungent mixture of chopped shrimp. Fish are drawn to the area as pieces of shrimp break off from the cage. Processed bait for ocean fishing.
A caddisfly-shaped lure crafted from a crow feather. Recommended for freshwater fly fishing novices.
A polished silver lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting fish. Especially effective in lakes.
The weight of this steel lure allows for casting great distances, such as from coastlines.
A heavy plug lure made to resemble a minnow. Effective in attracting fish from both surface and floor.
A freshwater fishing lure made from a snurble tuft.
The sheer weight of this steel lure allows for casting tremendous distances, such as from coastlines.
A metal river lure designed to resemble both a mayfly and a minnow, allowing for use in a variety of different situations.
A small metal cage packed with northern krill. Fish are drawn to the area as krill float off from the cage. Processed bait for ocean fishing.
A polished mythril lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting all manner of lake and marsh life.
A freshwater lure made from a wildfowl feather. Its uncanny resemblance to a mayfly makes it irresistible to vilekin-feeding fish such as trout.
A light freshwater lure crafted to resemble a frog. Best suited for larger prey such as pikes and certain trout.
A shiny blacklip oyster shell lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting all manner of aquatic life. Especially effective in lakes.
Several small spinners joined together to resemble a school of fish. Especially effective in rivers.
A freshwater fly designed to sink below the water's surface, and by doing so, attract the larger carnivorous fish living near the floor.
A curved man-made lure used traditionally in the Far East, the name means literally “bow horn.” Increases chances of landing a big catch, even when casting from shore.

Impress your friends with these beautiful leather-bound replicas of Lewphon of Sharlayan's crowning achievement in the field of history, theology, and astrology. Just do not allow those friends to open any of the volumes, as they are all blank.

Need to convince a special someone that you are deeply involved in a tangled web of international intrigue, so that they might keep you company in your chambers on what most certainly could be your last night amongst the living? A couple of official-looking documents can only help your ignoble cause.
All attempts to remove the mask of this goblin replica have failed, so do not even consider trying it yourself.
An expertly crafted replica of the Ultima Weapon. (Miniature Gaius van Baelsar sold separately.)
A commissioned oil painting of Cid Garlond, former engineer for the Garlean Empire and founder of the Garlond Ironworks. Original artist unknown.
A commissioned oil painting of realm-renowned agent of enquiry Hildibrand and his faithful assistant Nashu Mhakaracca. Original artist unknown.
A simple wall-mounted planter, perfect for flowers or miniature shrubs.

Impress your friends with these beautiful leather-bound replicas of naturalist Marcette Manne's comprehensive collection of knowledge. Just do not allow those friends to open any of the volumes, as they are all blank.
A chimney-less hearth designed to resemble those popular in the Far East. Do not forget proper ventilation while using.
A partition designed in the riviera fashion, but reaching only less than halfway to the ceiling so as to provide privacy without making the room feel smaller.
A pruned and potted umbrella fig tree.

A pruned and potted dragon tree. It is said that anyone in the presence of this breed of flora is unable to tell a lie, though it might also be that anyone in the presence of a dragon tree is unable to ask the hard questions.
A spherical map of the heavens based off of legendary Ishgardian astrologian Adaunel the Younger's lifetime of findings.
Woven from sweet-smelling rush grass, these rectangular floor mats are widely used in the Far Eastern land of Doma.
A low counter-type table crafted in an L shape.
A low partition outfitted with several planter pots.

A stylish floor lamp crafted from a rare Levin orb.
※One per estate only.

A stylish floor lamp crafted from a large Levin orb─now with more snap, crackle, and pop!
※One per estate only.

Grant boons and make decrees in style while lounging in this near-perfect replica of Emperor Xande's throne.
※One per estate only.
A welcome mat designed to complement riviera residences. Don't tread on me.
Made from the feathers of forty-leven geese, this large bed can hold approximately eight children, four hound dogs, and a piggy stolen from the shed.
A decorative pillar designed to resemble a chocobo.
A plush cushion upholstered in the riviera fashion.
A plush cushion upholstered in the glade fashion.
A plush cushion upholstered in the oasis fashion.

A simple stable large enough for keeping and raising as many chocobos as you can imagine (if 512 is the maximum number you can imagine).
※One per estate only.
An outdoor lantern traditionally placed outside one's home for the duration of the Moonfire Faire.
People hailing from the Far East claim that wishes written on small slips of parchment and tied to the bamboo will come true. (Magical wish parchment sold separately.)
This leafy shrub has been expertly pruned and trimmed into a perfect sphere.
A wooden garden partition outfitted with planter pots.
A ceramic pot filled with crystal-clear water and several water lilies.
A decorative outdoor pond encircled by smooth stones.
A blackened pot perfect for hanging over a cookfire.
Because sometimes there are things even a Roegadyn cannot reach.
Several flat smoothed stones arranged in a straight line.
Several flat smoothed stones arranged in a curving pattern.
Several thinly cut cross sections of a massive tree trunk arranged to form a straight path.
Several thinly cut cross sections of a massive tree trunk arranged to form a curved path.
A rectangular wooden box filled with blooming wildflowers.
A wooden bucket filled with crystal-clear water. Families in the Far East use these receptacles to chill fruit during the hot summer moons.
A living fence designed to complement glade residences. Mix and match at your own peril.
A decorated stone fence designed to complement oasis residences. Mix and match at your own peril.
A pointed iron fence designed to complement riviera residences. Mix and match at your own peril.
A flora-themed interior wall designed to complement riviera residences.
A flora-themed interior wall designed to complement glade residences.
A flora-themed interior wall designed to complement oasis residences.
Experience luxury living with this interior wall which features an elegant pattern adored by the Ul'dahn elite.
These striped walls are guaranteed to make your room appear thin...or fat.
An intricate interior wall crafted from countless tiny pieces of ceramic fit together in breathtaking patterns.
Simple, yet stylish, bisque flooring is perfect for the modern adventurer.
Carved from a single piece of beautiful marble, this floor is fit for a king (or queen).
Specialty flooring that is cool to the touch and easy to clean.
A massive lamp designed to resemble the villain of the Moonfire Faire─the Bombard.
A brilliant bauble pried from the Emperor Xande's colossal seat of rule.
A sphere of lightning-aspected energies encased in a transparent receptacle of hyperfused silica.
A perfect sphere of overcharged lightning-aspected energies encased in a transparent receptacle of hyperfused silica.
A durable sweet-smelling grass native to the Far East and used in the weaving of baskets and floor mats.
A unique type of flora which grows on inland ponds, its round, flat leaves creating a floating canopy on the water's surface.
A milky white flower commonly found growing in the humid climes of the southern seas.
Unlike those of tree-dwelling cloudkin, waterfowl feathers are exceptional at trapping in heat while keeping out water.
Silk that has been spun into lightweight balls that bear the appearance of cotton.
Each strand of mist silk is twice as thin as regular silk, making it much more difficult to work with.
This soft cloth has been treated with a thin layer of resin to repel water.
Glass treated with a complex alchemical concoction to reduce glare.
A thin, tiny plate of hammered wolfram.
A rock with an elemental aspect leaning unnaturally towards umbral.
An unforgettably pleasant-smelling log obtained in the Black Shroud.
A thin but sturdy construction material made by pressing together layers of wood, designed to achieve uniform strength. Several additional layers have been applied to the board to improve durability.
A hook masterfully wrought from darksteel and shaped to bear weight equally regardless of the direction in which it is pulled.
A roll of wire painstakingly drawn out from darksteel and combined with a second length of wire to enhance strength.
A complex cog masterfully wrought from rose gold.
A continuous strap of leather painstakingly wrought from gryphonskin and then treated with water to increase hardness.
A luxurious fabric woven from silver thread, featuring raised patterns more beautiful than anything ever seen in the realm.
An ultra-concentrated potent acid with myriad applications.

A zesty Near Eastern relish made by stewing tomatoes with select spices and seasoning. An extra turn of the sun over a cookfire has boiled off excess water, leaving a remarkably rich reduction sure to titillate the tongue.

A bitter fruit found growing in the Ixali homelands. While typically avoided by the Ixal themselves, it is a favorite amongst chocobos, and is known to deepen the red hues of their feathers.
A hard, bitter fruit found in the forests of Far Eastern Doma. It is a favorite amongst chocobos, and is known to lighten the red hues of their feathers.

A bitter fruit found growing in the arid soils of Mamook. While typically avoided by the Mamool Ja themselves, it is a favorite amongst chocobos, and is known to deepen the green hues of their feathers.
A bitter berry found growing on the distant Isle of Val. It is a favorite amongst chocobos, and is known to lighten the green hues of their feathers.
A bitter fruit found growing on the volcanic soil of O'Ghomoro. While typically avoided by the kobolds, it is a favorite amongst chocobos, and is known to deepen the blue hues of their feathers.
A bitter fruit found growing on the Cieldalaes─a remote archipelago in the Rhotano Sea. It is a favorite amongst chocobos, and is known to lighten the blue hues of their feathers.

A foul, bitter fruit found growing on the Near Eastern island of Thavnair. While typically avoided by the residents of Radz-at-Han, it is a favorite amongst chocobos, and is known to restore feathers to their original hue.
A bitter carrot-like root vegetable native to the Near East and a favorite amongst chocobos.
A pungent, tear-inducing vegetable that thrives in the alkali sands of Near Eastern Thavnair. It is a favorite amongst chocobos.

A fraction of the size, yet every bit as annoying as the real thing. Be forewarned: once Ultros shows up, he's liable to stick around.

Use item to acquire the Hoary the Snowman minion.

Currently, “baby fat” is the prevailing excuse for this cherubic chick's gigant-like girth.
Use item to acquire the heavy hatchling minion.

Despite convincing research by top academics from around the realm and beyond, most Miqo'te scholars refuse to believe that there may be some ancestral connection between their race and cats (fat or not).
Use item to acquire the fat cat minion.

This particular yeti is content in knowing that bigger is not always necessarily better.
Use item to acquire the Littlefoot minion.

Use item to acquire the mummy's little mummy minion.

There was an old betta who swallowed a fry. No one knows why it swallowed the fry, but for some reason, the fry can now fly.
Use item to acquire the assassin fry minion.

Legend states these strange creatures can only survive on land as long as the plate atop their heads remains wet.
Use item to acquire the water imp minion.

The Seventh Astral Era is secure as long as the Archon is ever at our sides.
Use item to acquire the wind-up Louisoix minion.

As with dark matter, zodium has the faculty to assimilate with other forms of matter, effectively restoring them to their original condition. However, unlike dark matter, which will bond only with certain materials depending on its purity, zodium appears to bond with almost everything, leading one to entertain the notion that this substance mayhap serves as one of the building blocks of all creation.

While some view this traditional Doman gardening technique as naught more than a reflection of man's arrogance in believing nature can be bent to his will, most simply find it a beautiful and calming form of art.
A precision instrument for telling time. Its towering silhouette adds a touch of gravitas to the ambience of any room.
A large bathtub designed in the Doman fashion.
A folding partition commonly found in Far East nations. Upon one side is a reproduction of an ancient Doman wall painting depicting a variety of beastkin in their natural habitat.
A table designed in the Doman fashion. The underside has been treated with strange Eastern magicks to emit heat during the winter months.
While far less nutritious than real vegetables, these wax replicas will look nicer in your pantry.
A counter designed to replicate those found in Adventurers' Guilds across Eorzea. This model comes complete with a built-in light that can be used to illuminate leve plates.
A Hatching-tide-themed floor lamp.

For the denizens of the Twelveswood, the consumption of tea is a means of relaxing the mind, allowing for uninhibited communion with nature.

Considered the most important of the day's seven meals (preceding both pre-midday mead and eleventh bell tarts), the Ul'dahn elite rarely miss this opportunity to gorge themselves before moving on to the next opportunity to gorge themselves.

This pile of parchment appears to be pages taken from <var 1A 02 /var>The Last Paean<var 1A 01 /var>─a detailed account of the life and times of a legendary bard who traveled the realm bringing joy to all he met. Strewn across one's bureau, the documents give any library or study a heightened air of sophistication.
A miniature wooden altar hung in Doman houses, allowing people to worship the gods within the privacy of their own homes.
Upon this ornamental scroll is painted the Doman character “jin,” meaning “mankind.”
A partition designed in the Doman fashion, reaching to the ceiling and so sturdy that it may as well be a wall.

“If the <var 1A 02 /var>man<var 1A 01 /var> who once owned the <var 1A 02 /var>chest<var 1A 01 /var> is now <var 1A 02 /var>dead<var 1A 01 /var>, he won't mind anyone else using it.” Such was the logic employed when removing this sturdy treasure coffer from Sastasha.
A barrel planter crafted from oak.

A decadent chocolate cake emblazoned with the House Valentione coat of arms.

A carved wooden podium not unlike the ones used by the Order of Nald'thal to deliver their sermons.

Far more bitter than its black counterpart, green tea is by far the beverage of choice in Far Eastern Doma. To offset the sharpness of its flavor, it is oft accompanied by something sweet, such as sticky rice cakes.

Have you dreamed of owning your very own well, but are plagued by one or more of the following psychological ailments: acrophobia, claustrophobia, aquaphobia, bathophobia, or cleithrophobia? Well fear no longer. This quality stone well, manufactured in Eorzea with 100% Eorzean materials, requires no hole to be dug, no ground to be sanctified, and no chain letters to be passed along to your dearest enemies.

A striking dummy designed in the Doman fashion.
※Up to three dummies may be placed in a single estate, regardless of type.
A variety of cherry tree from the Far East modified through generations of grafting and crossbreeding to bloom perpetually.
A square sheet of crimson-colored felt upon which dolls are displayed for Little Ladies' Day.
Outdoor lighting certain to heat up any relationship.
A green, leafy tree transplanted from an island in the Cieldalaes. The word “banana” is actually a bastardization of “pamama,” the term used in the fruit's native habitat.
A miniature astroscope used by aspiring astrologians to peer into the farthest reaches of the firmament.
A round outdoor table and matching chairs designed in the riviera fashion.

Though their beady eyes and awkward walk give them an air of unintelligence, dodos are actually quite clever creatures. A mother dodo will, when creating a nest, first dry grass in the sun for several days before adding it to the pile, so as to prevent the growth of molds harmful to her offspring.
A wooden receptacle for use by retainers to store goods entrusted for sale while protecting them from the elements. ※Can only be placed outdoors.
A wooden counter for use by retainers. ※Can only be placed outdoors.
An interior wall bespeckled with a hypnotically random pattern of colorful dots certain to drive any sane man to his wit's end.
An interior wall covered from top to bottom in colorful wavy lines certain to induce seasickness in even the most hardened sailor.
Woven from sweet-smelling rush grass, tatami flooring is the perfect complement to any home furnished in the Doman fashion.
Marble floor tiling alternately colored black and white.
Cobbles commonly used in Ul'dahn roadways and plazas.
Ceiling-mounted lighting expertly crafted to resemble the moon and stars.

A form of cinnabar known to contain traces of quicksilver.

Thinly sliced bamboo used to preserve the aroma of rare fragrant wood.

This freshwater amphibian is characterized by whorling patterns of deep amber across its moist skin.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

A tiny winged dragon only recently discovered in the Churning Mists.
[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

The lumpy shell of the lava snail is extremely heat resistant, protecting its tiny resident from otherwise unbearable temperatures.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

A massive freshwater squid found in the lakes of Coerthas.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.

Originally introduced to Doma by Ala Mhigan merchants, sukiyaki is a popular dish that consists of thinly sliced meat and vegetables cooked in sweet and savory soy-based sauce.

An alchemical potion concocted by mad scientists a thousand years dead. Some of the realm's more daring blacksmiths have applied the unnaturally viscous substance to a variety of weapons and found that it heightens the attributes of certain martial artifacts of ancient Allagan design. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.

An alchemical thread woven by mad scientists a thousand years dead. Some of the realm's more daring weavers have applied the unnaturally pliable substance to a variety of vestments and found that it heightens the attributes of certain martial artifacts of ancient Allagan design. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.

An alchemical potion concocted by mad scientists a thousand years dead. Some of the realm's more daring goldsmiths have applied the unnaturally illuminated substance to a variety of gems and found that it heightens the attributes of certain martial artifacts of ancient Allagan design. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.

A note of promise received from Rowena for the delivery of Allagan tomestones of creation or poetics. However, due to the House of Splendors changing its policies, it is now worth less than the paper on which it is scribed.

Though considerably different in construction, Garlond Ironworks engineers insist this bulky contraption serves the same purpose as a traditional tomestone, and is merely of an earlier, less efficient design. This particular variety is not as highly sought as it once was, and may no longer be exchanged for other wares.
The Kojin carve, from shell, idols such as this one to present as offerings to their exalted Lord of the Revel, Susano.
This pulsating metal idol forged in the likeness of the primal Lakshmi is thought to be employed by the Ananta in forbidden summoning ceremonies.

The fermenting of tea leaves is common practice in the Far East where tea is consumed multiple times a day. Fermentation is thought to enhance flavor while dulling the leaves' natural bitterness. Fermented leaves are pressed into bricks to save space when shipping.
Finely milled Gyr Abanian wheat.
A traditional source of protein in the Far East, tofu is made from curdled soy bean extract.
One of Far Eastern cuisine's five main seasonings, rice vinegar is slightly more sweet and mild than Aldenard's vinegars of popoto or apple.
A sweetener made by juicing sugar beets and then boiling the extract down until all the water has evaporated, leaving only a fine, grey powder.
Far Eastern rice wine prepared with other ingredients for use in cooking. Often added to seafood dishes to remove unpleasant aromas.
Cooking oil pressed from ruby cotton seeds. Its high flash point and lack of odor make it ideal for deep-frying.
A coagulant naturally found in seawater, commonly used in the Far East to make tofu.
A briny salt harvested by sun-drying then burning sea algae.
Unlike the drier varieties common in Aldenard and Ilsabard, this particular strand of Far Eastern rice becomes extremely sticky when cooked.
A nutty grain that can be substituted for flour in breads and noodles. Found across the Three Great Continents, but grown in abundance in the heart of Gyr Abania.

A sweet yet slightly tangy fruit with a thin skin and a fleshy orange interior. Can be found in the warmer valleys of Gyr Abania.

A greenish pink plum common across the eastern continent of Othard.

The root of the quick-growing kudzu vine is dug up and processed into kudzu powder which serves as a substitute for animal-based gelatins in Far Eastern desserts. It also is believed to exhibit healing properties, and can be found in most Hingan and Doman apothecaries.
While just as brilliantly purple, this Far Eastern cousin of the wizard eggplant is noticeably thinner, and thus requires less time to cook.
The spicy daikon radishes of Othard are known to grow as long and thick as a grown Hyur's forearm.
These tubers can be several times sweeter than most fruit, and as such are commonly processed into sugar for sweetening cakes and other confections.

Jhammel ginger's bulbous, aromatic roots can be sliced fresh and added to stews and seafood dishes to remove gaminess, ground and steeped in hot water to cure head colds, or dried and ground into a powder to use as a spice for breads and cookies.
Gyr Abanian carrots are not only longer, but a far deeper orange─nay, crimson─than those grown in central and western Eorzea.
Similar to green onions in flavor, the leeks of Gyr Abania are several times thicker, and far more piquant.
If removed from the ground when less than a fulm in length, bamboo shoots can be peeled and the fleshy interior eaten. A popular ingredient in Far Eastern stews and stir-fries.
Crisp mountain popotoes contain high quantities of starch that create a viscous paste when the tubers are ground. This paste can be eaten raw, fried into cakes, or added to stews for thickening.

These emerald legumes grow two to three beans per pod on stout bushes that are ready for harvest in the early fall. The beans are most often pressed into the milk which is used to make tofu, or fermented into various savory pastes and sauces.
These fungi native to the Far East are rarely eaten raw, the majority of those harvested dried, then used to make soup stock.
A pungent spice that can be used in seed form, or ground into a powder, enhancing the aroma tenfold.
Though they appear solid from the outside, the cylindrical root nodules of the lotus flower are riddled with holes, possibly to accommodate for the waterlogged environments in which the plant grows.
The sweet, tightly packed leaves of Othardian sun cabbages are deceptively sweet, making them perfect in salads or stews.
With an aroma similar to licorice, both the stalks and the seeds of this Othardian herb can be used to enhance the flavor of exotic Far Eastern dishes.
A close cousin to highland wheat, Gyr Abanian wheat has been improved by Ala Mhigan farmers over generations to increase both flavor and yield.

A hard, orange fruit common in eastern Othard. It is well known that seven summers must pass before a newly planted persimmon tree will bear fruit.
<var 48 F201F8 /var><var 49 F201F9 /var>EXP Bonus:<var 49 01 /var><var 48 01 /var> +3% <var 48 F201F8 /var><var 49 F201F9 /var>Duration:<var 49 01 /var><var 48 01 /var> 30m (Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)
While not edible, the leaves of the persimmon tree are oft used in the preservation of other food.
Clear water taken from a mountain spring on the eastern end of Abalathia's Spine.
Clear, odorless water taken from one of the many springs found on Othard's Fanged Crescent.
The unbearably tough shoulder meat of a steppe dzo.
A lean piece of meat taken from under the short ribs of an Othardian hornbill.
Heavy salting and spicing are methods commonly employed to remove the oft overpowering gaminess of this beastkin flesh.
A dark-haired variety of swine bred on Hingashi's Koshu island. Its carefully selected diet is believed to render its meat tender and its fat flavorful.
The massive egg of a gagana.

Compared to that of an aldgoat, marid, or deathmouse, the milk of a steppe dzo is high in fat and flavor.
<var 48 F201F8 /var><var 49 F201F9 /var>EXP Bonus:<var 49 01 /var><var 48 01 /var> +3% <var 48 F201F8 /var><var 49 F201F9 /var>Duration:<var 49 01 /var><var 48 01 /var> 30m (Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)
This edible seaweed can be consumed raw, or dried into paper-like squares and wrapped around sticky rice.

A distant cousin of malm kelp, Ruby Tide kelp is harvested and dried in the sun to enhance flavor. Squares of the seaweed are cut and steeped in boiling water to create one of the savory broths used in Hingan cuisine.
A variety of algae found in the Ruby Sea, commonly harvested for its salt.

Ink fortified with koppranickel sand to improve aetherial conductivity.
Ink fortified with durium sand to improve aetherial conductivity.
Ink fortified with palladium sand to improve aetherial conductivity.
This alchemically formulated potation accelerates the growth of foliage.
This alchemically formulated potation accelerates the growth of foliage.
An adhesive substance created by grinding down the chitinous carapaces of beetles and mixing it with heated pine resin.
These pinkish crystals grow naturally on the shores of Loch Seld.
A sticky substance secreted by pine trees when their limbs are cut.
A translucent liquid extracted from persimmon wood by steeping it in hot water. Used in the tanning of raw animal hides.
A brownish variety of the mineral used by leatherworkers to tan animal hides. It is only found in the mountains of Eastern Aldenard.
This Far Eastern perennial has a biting aroma that even many Othardians find off-putting.
This annual is coveted by perfumers for its honey-sweet aroma.
Though recognized as a weed, this winter annual is edible and will oft be harvested in the late months for use in various Doman and Hingan dishes.
Though recognized as a weed, this winter annual is edible and will oft be harvested in the late months for use in various Doman and Hingan dishes.
Named for the protruding buds from which its bright-yellow flowers bloom, nipplewort is a common winter annual whose leaves are gathered for use in Othardian cuisine.
When steeped in boiling water, the leaves of this rare perennial change color, turning a bright bluish green.
A herb with an aroma so heavenly, it will cleanse both your soul and your palate of ill flavors (or so say merchants who would see you buy their stock).
A herb with an aroma so heavenly, the gods themselves must have blessed it (or so say merchants who would see you buy their stock).
The curved horn of a muud suud.
The twisted horn of a gazelle.
The massive ebon horn of a steppe dzo.
The powdery scales of a giant moth's wing.
A single adult bombfish can have as many as a thousand of these lightweight-yet-sturdy spines jutting from its body.
The thick chitinous head of a rhino beetle, complete with eyes, antennae, and mandibles.
Processed beech lumber.
Processed larch lumber.
Processed persimmon lumber.
Processed zelkova lumber.
Processed torreya lumber.
A rough-cut log of beech timber.
A rough-cut log of larch timber.
A rough-cut log of persimmon timber.
A rough-cut log of zelkova timber.
A rough-cut log of torreya timber.
This glossy red coating, made from the sap of the lacquer tree, is used to both color and preserve wooden crafts.
The thick branch of a beech tree.
The thick branch of a torreya tree.
A small nugget of impure koppranickel.
A small nugget of impure high steel.
An ingot of smelted koppranickel.
An ingot of smelted high steel.
A small nugget of impure durium.
An ingot of Doman iron, smelted using Far Eastern techniques.
An ingot of smelted durium.

An ingot of smelted palladium.

Amber-colored sand consisting of tiny grains of koppranickel.
A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal koppranickel.
Jade-colored sand consisting of tiny grains of durium.
A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal Doman iron (also known as mochi iron for its resemblance to the Far Eastern rice cakes).
A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal durium.
Metallic sand consisting of tiny grains of Doman iron.
Silver-colored sand consisting of tiny grains of palladium.
A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal molybdenum.
A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal palladium.
A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal chromium.

Not to be outdone by their Near Eastern counterparts who perfected the aurum regis-hardening agent, Raziqcoat, several Far Eastern alchemists have joined together to create Domacoat─a substance capable of hardening palladium.
Not actually created from bones, this hot-burning fuel is the result of baking coal in an airless furnace at an extremely high temperature.
A yellow jewel.
A light-blue jewel.
A violet jewel.
A deep blue jewel.
Also known as “true jade,” this milky green stone is coveted by the Far Eastern elite.
A blood red jewel.
An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be triphane.
An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be kyanite.
An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be star spinel.
An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be azurite.
An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be imperial jade.
An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be rhodonite.
Several yalms of undyed, bright-red bloodhempen cloth wrapped around a short wooden distaff.
Coarse yarn spun from bloodhemp fiber.
A common grass found growing throughout Othard. From its stalks, bloodhempen yarn is created.
Several yalms of undyed ruby cotton cloth wrapped around a short wooden distaff.
Light yarn spun from ruby cotton.

The fibrous flower of a rare cotton plant that only grows <var 1A 02 /var>under<var 1A 01 /var> the Ruby Sea. As such, Eorzean scholars insist that the flora is in no way related to normal cotton, and is instead a unique variety of sea kelp.
Several yalms of undyed kudzu cloth wrapped around a short wooden distaff.
Thick, fibrous yarn spun from kudzu vines.

If allowed to grow unchecked, a single kudzu plant can cover an acre of forest in less than a single summer, blocking the sun from the plants it envelops. A large swath of the outer Black Shroud currently finds itself being slowly suffocated by the invasive weed.
Several yalms of undyed steppe serge wrapped around a short wooden distaff.
Soft, water-absorbent yarn spun from multiple varieties of hair sheared from beastkin of the Azim Steppe.
The regal mane of a halgai.
The long brown hair of a steppe manzasiri.
Though exhibiting a similar luster as normal silk, twinsilk is far more durable and resistant to discoloring.
A thin lustrous thread woven from countless silken strands pulled from a rare highland twincoon.
A massive cocoon spun by not one, but multiple highland erucas.

Cloth woven from the plant rhea. Due to the complexity of the spinning process, there are very few clothcrafters in the world who can produce this weave, making it extremely rare. Most known samples are in the possession of Far Eastern royalty.
A variety of ramie better suited to the climes of Far Eastern Othard.
Hempen cloth woven using age-old methods passed down for countless generations by Doman clothiers.
A large piece of cured gagana skin.
A large piece of cured gyuki hide.
A large piece of cured tiger skin.
A large piece of cured marid hide.
A large piece of cured gazelle hide.
A large piece of cured true griffin hide.
The rough skin of a majestic gagana.
The smooth hide of a devilish gyuki.
The striped skin of a ferocious tiger.
The thick hide of a mammoth marid.
The bristly hide of a steppe gazelle.
The downy hide of a true griffin.
Forbidden in many markets for the nefarious means with which it is extracted, this wax is cherished by leatherworkers for the luster it brings to tanned hides when applied.
Geological scholars claim that this sedimentary stone is actually comprised of the shells of thousands upon thousands of tiny sea creatures.
Unlike other sedimentary stone, slate has been compressed under the weight of mountains for so long that it is surprisingly hard, making it ideal for whetstones and grinding stones.
A whetstone carved from slate. Used for sharpening metal or stone blades.
A blackish mineral possibly containing trace amounts of the precious stone tourmaline.
A strange, pearlescent volcanic rock that expands tenfold upon heating in a kiln or forge.
A garnet-like mineral that, due to its extreme hardness, is used in grinding wheels.
A soft, clay-like soil believed to be formed of compacted yellow dust carried on the wind from faraway lands.
The elementally aspected remnants of aetherially reduced matter. This fine sand emits a weak glow indiscernible at gloaming.
The elementally aspected remnants of aetherially reduced matter. This fine sand emits a weak glow indiscernible at dawn.
The elementally aspected remnants of highly concentrated aetherially reduced mineral matter.
The elementally aspected remnants of highly concentrated aetherially reduced mineral matter.
The elementally aspected remnants of highly concentrated aetherially reduced mineral matter.

Though king of the five seas and beyond, scholars classify the liopleurodon with scalekin rather than wavekin.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

A freshwater fish named for its long, ribbon-like fins that it uses to both attract prey and distract predators.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

This large carnivorous specimen is native to the southeastern reaches of the One River where the waters run slow and deep.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

The beauty of this small freshwater fish native to Yanxia is oft compared to the angels of ancient eastern scripture.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Like most saltwater eels, the blackfin snake eel of the Ruby Sea is a nocturnal hunter.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

These tiny fish commonly found in the many shallow tributaries feeding into the upper One River rarely grow beyond a few ilms in length.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Despite their small size, sweatfish prefer the swift rapids of the One River's northern tributaries for the cover it provides them from predators.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

By no means the most winsome of wavekin, the rock saltfish has adapted to survival in the saline waters of Loch Seld.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Near the bottom of the food chain, swift-swimming comet minnows serve as food for many of the larger fish that swim the waters of the Hathoeva and Velodyna rivers.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

This common variety of freshwater carp is found up and down the One River.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Named after the Hingan warriors whose grace and elegance in battle resemble the means by which this wavekin swims the turbid depths of the One River.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

This bright-yellow fish is native to Gyr Abania and found in both the Hathoeva and Velodyna rivers, sometimes as far west as East End.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A small-yet-plump fish most commonly found in Hak Khaal, one of the One River's many narrow steppe tributaries.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

The Yat goby is an eel-like bottom dweller named after the Azim Steppe tributary in which it is most commonly found.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Similar to a bass in appearance and flavor, the similarities end there, with this variety of meagre preferring the coastal waters of the Ruby Sea and the Glass Ocean to fresher rivers and lakes.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

This distant relative to the carp can be found hunting the waters of the Hathoeva and Velodyna rivers.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Some say this Ruby Sea shark earned its name from sailors long out of port who, upon seeing the shark's pale skin cresting above the waves, would reminisce of their favorite pleasure boat courtesan.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

This queer horse-like wavekin swims upright, using two tiny fins near its head to slowly swim through the waters of extreme salinity it calls home.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

This freshwater specimen of minuscule proportions can be found in almost any river and lake from central to eastern Othard.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Scholars are divided as to whether this wavekin native to the Ruby Sea and Glass Ocean is in fact a snake or an eel.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Groupers gather in swift currents of the Ruby Sea and the Rasen Kaikyo to feed on the abundant life drawn to the area.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

This violent scalekin has the jaws of a carpenter's vise. Many a careless fisher has lost a fingertip or three when navigating the snapper-rich waters of Loch Seld.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

Remarkably similar in appearance to a shark, it is believed this salt lake fish periodically exposes its dorsal fin above the water's surface to frighten land predators such as bears.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

Prehistoric drawings of this salt lake fish have been discovered on cave walls throughout Gyr Abania, suggesting that this particular species has endured at least six umbral eras.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

The Abalathian bitterling's ivory white skin easily distinguishes it from its silver cousins also found in the freshwater rivers and lakes of Gyr Abania.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

One of only a few freshwater sharks discovered in Eorzea, the steelshark can primarily be found in the rivers and lakes of Gyr Abania.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Though a cousin to the Hak bitterling, the waters of Tao Khaal have taken the Tao bitterling on a slightly different evolutionary path.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

This large goby uses its natural black and brown mottling to conceal itself in the sandy bed of the Slow Wash.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Called “akame” or “red eye” in the Far East for the unique color of this freshwater fish's optical organs.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

This freshwater fish is known to change the color of its skin come spawning season.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

This saltwater fish has a distinct crimson coloring that makes it popular amongst aquarium owners.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A delicious, fatty freshwater fish native to the Velodyna and Hathoeva rivers.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

A unique variety of freshwater charr found only in the waters near Heather Falls.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A plump freshwater wavekin with pearlescent scales and a name that sounds better than the fish tastes.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

The pale yellow glow emitted by this freshwater fish is believed to be caused by unbalanced levels of aspected aether in the wavekin's humours.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

The pale blue glow emitted by this freshwater fish is believed to be caused by unbalanced levels of aspected aether in the wavekin's humours.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Similar to the sea horse, the hanatatsu swims “standing,” though instead of resembling a beast of burden, this saltwater fish has taken on the appearance of a sprig of coral.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

A wildly misnamed freshwater crab with a highly durable carapace.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A remarkable crystalline fragment within which can be seen images from another world. Though such articles were once considered highly valuable, demand has dried up, leaving them with little value as bartering materials.

A dissolving agent concocted by Doman artisans that, when applied to certain weapons, heightens their attributes by removing impurities on their surface. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.
A durable thread used by Doman artisans. When woven into certain armor, it is believed to heighten its attributes. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.

A slightly corrosive paste concocted by Doman goldsmiths that, when applied to certain accessories, heightens their attributes by restoring their luster. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.

A note of promise received from Rowena for the delivery of Allagan tomestones of mendacity or poetics. However, due to the House of Splendors changing its policies, it is now worth less than the paper on which it is scribed.

Garlond Ironworks engineers believe this device to be an attempt by Allagan scientists to increase tomestone capacity, while keeping overall size relatively small. This may have become the next standard in tomestone data storage...had not their civilization been inconveniently wiped from the realm. This particular variety is not as highly sought as it once was, and may no longer be exchanged for other wares.

Required level: 70. IL: 375. Weapon type determined by current job or class at time of opening. Cannot be opened in instanced areas such as dungeons, PvP areas, or raids.
Comprising the front end of a shark-class submersible, this bow has been reinforced to double as a battering ram for subduing unruly sea creatures.
Comprising the top of a shark-class submersible, the bridge houses all of the equipment necessary for the vessel's crew to navigate the unplumbed depths of the Ruby Sea and beyond.

Comprising the center of a shark-class submersible, this ovoid hull is multi-walled to stabilize and maintain pressure within so that the vessel's crew does not succumb to the crushing weight of the waters it navigates. Several sturdy rudder fins serve to increase maneuverability.
Comprising the rear end of a shark-class submersible, this stern contains the unique independent engine which propels the craft.
Unlike the bows of most submersibles, the unkiu-class model is outfitted with rudder fins usually relegated to the stern.
Designed by the Onishishu─a collective of skilled Far Eastern craftsmen─this submersible bridge differs dramatically in build from those built in the West.

Comprising the center of an unkiu-class submersible, this ovoid hull is multi-walled to stabilize and maintain pressure within so that the vessel's crew does not succumb to the crushing weight of the waters it navigates. Supplemental propulsion engines have been affixed to the sides to increase underwater speed.
Comprising the rear end of an unkiu-class submersible, this stern contains a double propeller engine.

A sizable catch found primarily in the freshwater highland rivers of Gyr Abania.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

A deadly saltwater breed that protects itself with a pair of needle-like fins and a nigh-impenetrable coat of translucent scales.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

This land turtle can easily be identified by both its pointed shell and its powerful bite.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

A large freshwater fish that has─surprise─a distinct red tail fin.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

This crafty cephalopod can be found all along the Ruby Sea coastline─usually in the belly of some Hingan fisher who has eaten the creature raw and with a splash of soy sauce and citrus.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

The saltmill is believed to be an ancient sea specimen which adapted to life in hypersalinated waters after being transplanted into Loch Seld after the Sixth Umbral Calamity.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

From afar, this freshwater fish can appear to be a piece of floating woodland debris. Up close, it looks like a fish.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A unique petal-shaped maw and ribbon-like body distinguish this saltwater eel from more common varieties.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

The pale red glow emitted by this freshwater fish is believed to be caused by unbalanced levels of aspected aether in the wavekin's humours.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Despite the beard-like ventral fins which give this freshwater wavekin an aged look, gourami only have an average lifespan of three to five summers.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

An authentic reproduction of the Heavensturn decoration displayed at homes and places of business.
An authentic reproduction of an official Valentione's Day announcement. Without proper advertisement, some may mistake Valentione's Day for any other day, albeit one with far more pink balloons.

An authentic reproduction of festive Valentione's Day balloons created by drying, coloring, then stamping the bladders of various flying fish caught in the Sea of Clouds with the House Valentione coat of arms. The bladders are then filled with heated air to keep them afloat.
An authentic reproduction of a tiered dais used in the Far East to display dolls. Adapted in Eorzea for use on Little Ladies' Day.
An authentic reproduction of a pushcart filled with thousands upon thousands of fragrant roses (give or take a few thousand).
This peculiar contraption creates illusions by weaving together myriad shades of light. Used during Hatching<var 1F /var>tide for celebratory purposes.
A long-lasting synthetic resin concocted by Radz-at-Han's finest alchemists. Used as both an adhesive as well as a varnish.
A coarse-grained abrasive concocted by Radz-at-Han's finest alchemists. Used to restore the luster of even the most corroded metals.
A traditional Near Eastern weave that keeps its wearer cool while protecting her from the harsh rays of the sun.
Quarried from Thavnair's towering sea cliffs, this mineral is prized by leatherworkers for its use in tanning hides.
Countless Hannish alchemists have chosen death over revealing the secret recipe of this odorless paste used in the creation of some of the island nation's most valuable armor.
Iron ore that has been exposed to the waters of a mineral spring, and undergone significant changes to both color and chemical makeup.
A sizable piece of rock containing traces of a precious metal known as silvergrace.
A rough-cut log of black willow timber.
A distant cousin to the flax found in the highlands of Coerthas, the stalk of this fibrous plant is used to create a yarn known in Hingashi as “true linen.”
The coarse, bristly hide of a giant ground sloth.

Unlike those attached to non-imitation windows, these louvered shutters will ever remain pristine as they add a touch of the rustic to your interior décor.
This set for aspiring culinary artists includes soft, child-safe replicas of everything one might need in the kitchen, including a helpful Miqo'te poissonnier.
Spare a thought for the poor carpenter who toiled to make this furnishing both simple and elegant as you inevitably pile as many objects as physically possible atop its shelves.
A knitter's work is never done. In this case, literally.
An adventurer never leaves home without his compass! And his waterskin. And his lantern. And his potions. And his telescope. And his books. Really, an adventurer needs to learn to pack a bit lighter.
This storage unit is packed with enough spices, herbs, oils, and other ingredients to satisfy even the most dedicated culinarian.
One could raise an entire army of ducks with this much bread. Hypothetically.
For weary adults who have spent overmuch on alligator pears and cannot afford to live alone.
A large and lovely woven vessel. Be advised that if a Lalafell fits in it, she will sits in it.
Home is where the heap of unfolded undergarments is.
There's no better way to vaunt your wealth than buying three nearly identical pairs of trousers and refusing to wear any of them.
Opaque vessels of assorted size, perhaps containing flour and sugar. Or cookies. Or bugs.
Dishes for those with simple tastes and many friends.
A half-dozen goblets for fancy parties. Cupbearer not included.

Such neatly folded and extraordinarily fluffy towels can only have been purloined from an expensive inn.

A lubricant concocted by a certain Garlond Ironworks consultant that, when applied to weapons of similar origin, heightens their attributes by smoothing interactions between their many interlocking parts. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.

This particular variety is not as highly sought as it once was, and may no longer be exchanged for other wares.

There are enough sequins, spangly things, and assorted frippery here to turn even the plainest of scullery maids into a dazzling songbird. Provided that she can actually sing, that is.

To decorate an airship to the exacting standards of Eulmoran high society, only the finest of handcrafted ornamentation using the most opulent of materials will suffice. Provided that no one looks too closely, the contents of this crate should pass muster.
These delightful trinkets serve as perfect conversation pieces, though the designs vary significantly depending on what random odds and ends happened to be available at the time of creation.
Once the dense coal has been ground into powder and mixed with water, it can be used as a substitute for ink. Be sure to keep it away from white clothing, as the stains are a bugger to get out.
This selection of rare varieties of salt and spices native to Amh Araeng can be used to add a dash of elegance and a pinch of class to even the most unappetizing of dishes.

Every region of Norvrandt is, for some reason, blessed with an astonishing variety of glittering, shimmering, sparkling, and otherwise shiny stones. Il Mheg is no exception, as is amply demonstrated by these fine specimens.

In the hands of an artisan, these bits and pieces gathered from around Amh Araeng will eventually become the decorations used to adorn Eulmore's fleet of airships. In fact, it took another sort of artisan to even find them in the first place, having been forced to separate the proverbial wheat from the chaff in some of the desert's most perilous locations.

While not everything included in this assortment of locally sourced materials could be considered valuable, the various items combine to convey the very essence of Kholusia. This could, however, be attributed to the pungent oceanic odor they all seem to share.

Perhaps one day, these humble materials will fulfill their dream of being turned into flyers to advertise Eulmore's finest drinking and ogling establishment. With your help, this dream may very well come true.
An artisan's touch is required to turn this hodgepodge into something the Beehive's kitchen staff can use to produce its reasonably priced and reasonably tasty fare.
As sparkly and fabulous as these assorted materials may be, they have a long way to go before they can be added to the costume worn by the Beehive's songstress.

Few could envision that these rather uninspiring objects will eventually be soaring gracefully through the skies. Strictly speaking, it will be the airship to which they are attached that will be doing the flying, but it still counts.

As anyone who has had the dubious pleasure of visiting a seaside tourist trap can attest, the majority of the souvenirs sold are made from cheap and readily available materials, often found washed up on the shore along with the driftwood and dead jellyfish. The contents of this bag are─as is tradition─of similar ilk, clearly indicated by the dried seaweed with which most of the items are covered.

A dented artifact collected from the Copied Factory. At one time, avid and eccentric collectors would have paid a king's ransom for it, but such numismatic baubles have fallen out of style. Glory to mankind.
This gleaming idol of unknown provenance is carved in the shape of a very, very, very small Alexander.
This particularly clever invention relies on a fish's natural tendency to snag its face on spinning, jagged objects.
Botanists would no doubt be fascinated and confused in equal measure by this inexplicably effervescent potted plant.
The shirts placed upon this shelf are perfectly folded, and woe betide he who disturbs them in the name of trying one on.
A chair in the classical elven style.
A table in the classical elven style.
This sofa is so luxurious that you will never want to get up─and nor will you be able to on those particularly warm days when your skin practically fuses to it.
A softly glowing light fixture crafted to resemble one of the many lovely flowers in the pixies' home.
A cute cushion designed to resemble a popular pastry.
A large, rectangular section of wooden decking, complete with low fences, flower baskets, and a table laid with tea for two.

A whestone carved from alumina. Used for sharpening metal or stone blades.
This thinly spun glass is remarkably resistant to breakage, even when handled by a particularly clumsy craftsman.
A partially congealed ball of sticky sap extracted from a sandalwood tree.
A decent-sized piece of rock containing the precious metal beryllium.
Whatever it does, it does it sublimely.

A variety of mussel with coloring so stygian that it appears almost to have been steeped in shadow. A mussel of darkness, if you will. ...Become what you mussel.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A sumptuous serving of delectable mussels smothered in an oily garlic sauce, each one a perfectly bite-sized burst of flavor.

A highly concentrated elixir blended on the island of Kholusia.
A note of promise received for the delivery of facet equipment.
A detailed outline of complex crafting techniques. One delineation is consumed when using a specialist action.
Sturdy enough to support the weight of several large Roegadyn. Until it isn't.
At this stage, it is anyone's guess what this alloy will become. If it is extremely lucky, it may even end up as a door knocker.
Unless a skilled blacksmith or armorer can intervene, this steel is doomed to spend eternity as a useless metal square.
Even the skybuilders themselves are not quite sure what goes into these ingots, although the general consensus is that it is nothing valuable.
Leather made <var 1A 02 /var>for<var 1A 01 /var> skybuilders, not <var 1A 02 /var>from<var 1A 01 /var> them. Apparently.
How long is a length of rope? In this particular rope's case, this long.

Used for writing in ledgers to keep track of who is owed what. Considering the scale of the Ishgardian restoration, it is expected that a fair few bottles will be exhausted before the work is completed.
By all accounts, this plant-based milk has a pleasant enough taste, though Ishgardian culinarians have yet to succeed in efforts to turn it into cheese.
Surprisingly maneuverable, even when loaded with bricks and such.
Thankfully, this is a handful of <var 1A 02 /var>metal<var 1A 01 /var> nails, not ones grown from the fingers of the skybuilders themselves. That would be far less pleasant.
Those with a penchant for having little bits of metal sticking out from every surface in sight will be delighted to receive these carefully crafted metal studs.
An object without a clear purpose but will “probably come in handy one day,” as hoarders of useless junk are wont to say.
Can be attached to the handles of tools to allow them to be hung from belts and so forth, though care should be taken while walking to avoid having them flailing around wildly.
It seems this cloth is destined to become part of a comfortable couch, or perhaps a nice set of drapes.
Used in the preparation of several varieties of Ishgardian cooking and, on some occasions, as a condiment.
Uncooked pasta that is perfect for eating during construction. If you like uncooked pasta.
The expression “a barrel of laughs” was never meant to be taken literally, though if it were, one could fit a fair few in this voluminous wooden container.
In days to come, this most versatile of tools will become the bane of every nail that dared to stick out. And the occasional thumb.
In times of war, this metallic item of cookware can double as a makeshift helmet, provided the wearer has an unnaturally large head.
It almost seems a shame to cover this in layers of melted wax, though sadder still would be a candelabra without a candle.
The eventual owner of this majestic piece of thick cloth will be as snug as a bug in a rug. Or on a rug, to be precise.
As the saying goes, “A new broom sweeps clean,” though the person wielding said broom is also due at least some of the credit for any increase in cleanliness that may result.
The recipients of the other items in your inventory would probably prefer that you refrained from carrying loose pieces of charcoal about your person.
As is tradition with tea brewed for builders, it contains enough sugar to make the spoon stand on end.
Though one should avoid putting other people on a pedestal, the placement of inanimate objects should not pose any problems.
It is not only double-edged blades that cut both ways.
Considering that it lacks the ability to count anything whatsoever, “counter” seems to be something of a misnomer.
If the time you have spent in Ishgard has taught you anything, it is that the locals <var 1A 02 /var>really<var 1A 01 /var> like stone.
Ideal for leaping from scaffold to scaffold as one merrily frolics about the construction site, while others go about their backbreaking labor.
Any Ishgardian with any sense will already own a pair of gloves, but for those who do not, these will be a welcome gift.
Be careful to whom you give this. They may think you are trying to tell them something.

Though the recipe states that this mysterious concoction can cure any ailment, one must remember that it will under no circumstances reattach dismembered fingers, which is a remarkably common complaint among the skybuilders.
Children who fail to heed the word of their parents will be sent here without any supper.

In many Ishgardian residences, the oven doubles as a means of heating the house, with the occupants finding themselves subconsciously drawn to the kitchen during the colder months. Which is all of them.

Of all the items you have managed to stow about your person, this surely ranks as one of the largest and most cumbersome. Even the most proficient of aetherochemists would be baffled by the unsolved mystery of your impossibly deep pockets.
Not only can this be used for the cooking of various dishes, it also works wonders in the prevention of frostbite, as many residents of the Brume will attest.

Designed to be worn on top of other layers of clothing to protect them from dust and dirt and provide additional protection against the cold. Since Ishgardians tend to wear several layers of clothing to begin with, these overalls are cut much larger than those worn in warmer climes.
Serves to keep out not only water, but wind as well, though the cold inevitably finds a way through eventually.
One of many concoctions that serves little purpose on its own, but can be mixed with others for a variety of effects upon consumption, the large majority being some sort of agonizing death.
One unfortunate rail was left to stew in its own juices after finding its way into the pot. Literally.
The distinct lack of trees is one of many problems the first people to settle in Ishgard chose to ignore, making this otherwise commonplace material─sourced from the East Shroud─extremely valuable.
While this may look much like any other iron ore found in middle La Noscea, there are subtle differences that only an expert in the field will recognize. The name, for one, is considerably longer.
This sand gathered in central Thanalan is not only fine, but extremely well-behaved, choosing to stay in one closely knit lump while jostling alongside the rest of your possessions.

Though this hardy plant can grow almost anywhere, the snow-blasted precipices of Ishgard have so far proven too steep a challenge for it to overcome. This particular specimen was harvested in lower La Noscea, an environment far more conducive to plant life─or any sort of life, for that matter.
Ash! A-Ah! Savior of the Firmament!♪
Although upper La Noscea seems rather a distant location from which to source something as simple as salt, the Ishgardians are nothing if not particular in their tastes.

The electrum ore found in upper La Noscea is believed to be far better suited to the skybuilders' needs than any other variety. Were anyone to ask them why, they would, in most cases be met with a response along the line of, “Because it just is.”

The tradition of measuring powdered substances in units of “pinches” has been the cause of many arguments, largely due to differences in finger size between the various races. Folk in eastern Thanalan, where this sample was gathered, have been known to ask Lalafells to measure when selling, and Roegadyn when buying, for obvious reasons.
It is a well known fact among botanists that the flax in the South Shroud is superior to every other kind, for reasons far too complicated and boring for anyone else to care about.

Having only traveled the relatively short distance from the Coerthas central highlands to Ishgard, this spring water is still remarkably fresh, though the icy chill threatens to freeze it inside the bottle.
Few members of the mortal races are equipped to make the perilous journey to the Churning Mists, and those who do normally hope to have more than a log or two to show for their troubles.
Why the skybuilders would specify that their straw be brought from the Dravanian forelands is anyone's guess. Perhaps the smell helps their chocobos sleep more peacefully?
The time spent mining this ore in the Dravanian hinterlands would perhaps have seemed less arduous if you had the faintest idea how the skybuilders plan to use it.
You have a sneaking suspicion that you may have lost some of the sand during the return journey from the Sea of Clouds, though the amount you have in your possession should still suffice.
The thought of happy skybuilders drinking delicious tea was the only motivation you needed as you risked life and limb gathering these leaves in the Sea of Clouds.
There are easier places to collect spring water than the Dravanian forelands, though it seems your personal safety is not especially high on the skybuilders' list of concerns.

Compared to most places in Gyr Abania, the Peaks has more than its fair share of trees, so who would object to you taking a few logs? Bloodthirsty Qiqirn and rampaging ruud suuds, that's who. Or perhaps they just see you as an easy meal?

The Ruby Sea is not especially well known as a prime location for mining, though those who are nautically minded can uncover all sorts of rare and unique treasures. Whether the skybuilders choose to turn this into fine jewelry or something more mundane, like a tea strainer, remains to be seen.

Venomous snakes are something of a rarity in Ishgard, so the skybuilders have ordered that some be delivered from the Azim Steppe to help improve morale. Workers displaying a lack of enthusiasm will be given some time in “the pit” to rediscover their commitment to the cause.
While the Lochs are better known as a source of salt, the rich veins of ore are drawing in miners from far and wide.
Yanxia is rich in both flora and fauna, and horsetail forms a major part of the diet of many grazing creatures.

When an Ishgardian culinarian stated that her latest dish needed a pinch of salt, the skybuilders sought out the very best, though perhaps more than a single pinch would be required to make the lengthy journey to the Lochs worthwhile.

While water from the Ruby Sea may not sound particularly appealing, this was actually brought from a small freshwater spring on one of the surrounding islands. Drinking this is unlikely to result in life-threatening dehydration.
A pinch of anything tends not to be an awful lot, though this particular sand from the Azim Steppe is apparently worth more than its weight in gold.

Quite why a particular type of vine that can only be found in the Azim Steppe is necessary to the skybuilders' plans has yet to be explained. Perhaps they are planning to surprise you with a work of surpassing genius? Or perhaps not.
Obviously, none of the skybuilders has even heard of the Rak'tika Greatwood, though the specific qualities they seek in their timber can most easily be found in the white ash trees that grow there.
If a porous rock from the bottom of the ocean is required in the rebuilding of Ishgard, then so be it. Your job is to mine, not question the reasoning behind such dubious demands.
Why submit a boring chunk of gold ore when you can bring one all the way from Il Mheg instead?

This cotton must be very special indeed for you to bring it all the way from Lakeland in the First. You can only hope that the skybuilders appreciate you going the extra malm. And traveling to another world.

One day, this poor lizard is chasing other, smaller scurrying creatures across the desert plains of Amh Araeng, and the next, it is being transported to another world and dragged lashing and kicking to Ishgard. The chances of the cold-blooded scalekin being content in its frozen new surroundings are slim at best, and you can only hope that the skybuilders are grateful to you for supplying a miserable and motionless lizard.
Were the other contributors to hear that you traveled to Amh Araeng in the First simply to procure wheat, they would think you are just trying to show off.

The isle of Kholusia is known by the inhabitants of Norvrandt to have the very finest of gold sand. Whether this is up to the impossibly high standards of the skybuilders will only become apparent when it is submitted for inspection.
Any water gathered from Il Mheg is likely to have been enchanted by either the pixies or the Fuath, though that is a problem for the skybuilders, not you, to worry about.

Thankfully, the resin appears to have suffered no ill effects during your return from the Rak'tika Greatwood, meaning that it is still a gelatinous blob with seemingly no practical application whatsoever.

Timeworn pages of sheet music containing the full score for Hades's theme, <var 1A 02 /var>Invincible<var 1A 01 /var>.
A particularly glossy and durable variety of leather, the production of which is no mean feat.

The most advanced technology of the Skysteel Manufactory went into the creation of this block of metal. According to Biggs, equipment made from this material will allow its user to see around corners.

The most advanced technology of the Skysteel Manufactory went into the creation of this piece of leather. According to Biggs, equipment made from this material will allow its user to hear sounds before they are made.

The most advanced technology of the Skysteel Manufactory went into the creation of this bolt of cloth. According to Biggs, equipment made from this material will allow its user to smell a person's thoughts from a malm away.
While there seems to be an endless supply of these in Yanxia, why anyone would actually want them is unclear. They have a taste to match their appearance, in other words, revolting.
The ocean depths are dark and full of horrors... But also, rather a good location to harvest salt. Just watch out for the horrors.

A potted conifer displayed in homes during the Starlight Celebration. Its snowy color will make your décor sumptuous─and your gatherings lively as you argue with friends and neighbors over whether it is superior to the more traditional green. It is not known how long ago it was placed in its ceramic prison, and some attribute its unnatural longevity to it having formed a blood pact with a voidsent, which may be unlikely considering its distinct lack of blood.

Festive treats for those who prefer to express their Starlight spirit through eating until they lose consciousness. While one may be forgiven for mistaking these for leftovers from a previous year, that could not be further from the truth, according to their baker.
※Cannot be retrieved once used. ※Can be used up to 10 times.

This indoor frosty snowman will never melt away. He'll be there forever. Watching. Waiting. Authentically.
The detritus of many happy Starlight Celebration surprises. They may be empty, but at least they are <var 1A 02 /var>authentically<var 1A 01 /var> empty.
A large-scale reproduction of the piece entitled “Scions of the Seventh Dawn.”

What is worse than being born a toad? Being born a toad and then carried against your wishes from your home in western Thanalan to icy Ishgard, where if you don't freeze to death, are likely to be chopped up and boiled in a pot. That is what is worse. Much worse, in fact.
A horn that emits a primal sound that summons forth your hulking ufiti.

Water collected from a natural fount said to be blessed by Ox'Dalan, guardian of the underworld.

Savory-sweet and nourishing, this ant egg will have any Qitari exclaiming “Splendid!”
※Only for use in Qitari society quests. ※Not included in the gathering log.

Dwelling in rocky areas, this scorpion is splendidly hardy and promises to impart this quality to those who devour it.
※Only for use in Qitari society quests. ※Not included in the gathering log.

An ingredient used by the Qitari to make their splendid perfumes.
※Only for use in Qitari society quests. ※Not included in the gathering log.

Though splendid to behold, this mineral is quite toxic─but for Qhoterl Pasol's purposes, that too may be considered splendid.

Anyone hoping to use this oil in its raw state to close wounds and heal grazes will be left sorely disappointed, and perhaps just sore.

While the Qitari use this rare substance as an ingredient in cleansing solutions, some suspect that it merely masks odors rather than eliminating them. Several members of the community rub this on the more pungent areas of the body as a substitute to proper washing, a practice that is largely frowned upon.
※Only for use in Qitari society quests. ※Not included in the gathering log.

While clay is a common enough material, only the truly splendid is used in the repair of broken pots and such, as the Qitari tend to be rather fussy about such matters.
※Only for use in Qitari society quests. ※Not included in the gathering log.

When this rare mineral is ground down and made into ink, it can be used in a variety of artistic pursuits, such as calligraphy and so forth. Unfortunately, this particular sample is destined for a far more mundane purpose: the logging of excavated trinkets. To make matters worse, most Qitari have exceptionally poor handwriting.
※Only for use in Qitari society quests. ※Not included in the gathering log.

This splendid rock salt is sprinkled on meat during the smoking process to draw out its natural flavor. The same could, in fact, be said for practically any salt, but the Qitari tend to notice when someone tries to fob them off with anything less than the genuine article, hence the need to seek out this particular variety.
※Only for use in Qitari society quests. ※Not included in the gathering log.

Not to be confused with salt. Or Peter, whoever that is.

Countless years of weathering have produced a stone full of holes that produce a most splendid sound when air passes through them.

To maintain the splendid sheen of the stone tablets, one must use stones to polish stone.
※Only for use in Qitari society quests. ※Not included in the gathering log.

Suffused with magical energy, this stone can be used to make a trap as deadly as it is splendid.
※Only for use in Qitari society quests. ※Not included in the gathering log.

Packed with splendid nutrients, any who consume this worm will become as hardy as the rocks it dwells within.
※Only for use in Qitari society quests. ※Not included in the gathering log.

Only the most splendid picks will suffice for the Stewards, and to make those only the most splendid and densest ore will do.

Bones tend to make splendid lures, especially when one seeks to catch splendid fish.
