[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Business in the front. Sirensong in the back.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Perhaps this puffer could equip a racket and fur armguards and depart on a grand adventure. Or perhaps it's just a fish.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Warning: not an actual musical instrument. Do not attempt to blow on it.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Proof that anything looks friendlier when it has Matanga features, even sharks.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

This coelacanth took to the spectral currents out of dissatisfaction with the evolutionary hand it was dealt─including, perhaps, its distinct lack of hands.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

While known to scavenge the flesh of the drowned, this large grey shark will as surely feast upon the living.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

These rainbow-colored mollusks are believed to come from mermaids. Alas, not a one has ever been sighted, suggesting they have no desire to explore up where we walk, up where we run, up where we stay all day in the sun.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A squid whose head and mind are both as sharp as an arrow. It puts little thought into its diet, however, and will eat anything it can sink its barbed beak into.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

A shrimp known for its vibrant and resilient pink shell, as well as its long, sharp pincers.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

A long-lived fish that makes its home in the deepest recesses of the ocean.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

A variety of anglerfish thought to be breath spilled from a siren's lips.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Though this ancient sea-dweller lacks a powerful bite, it makes up for it with the ability to bludgeon and grind its prey against rocks.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

This doppelganger of the deep is able to mimic prey using its tentacles as it approaches. The psychological trauma of being attacked by oneself─or perhaps a loved one that relatives would jokingly call one's twin─often paralyzes the victim as the impostopus feeds.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

A beautiful jade-colored crustacean that is the envy of many a sea creature.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

An ancient wavekin allegedly born of divine error─or divine clumsiness, at the least.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Respected and feared by the peoples of the south sea isles, this ancient sea creature is the subject of myriad myths and legends.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

Hingan merchants will offer fragrant samples of these toothsome fish when they do not care to haggle with their patrons, and thus its name has entered the local lexicon to refer to a misleading statement.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Legend has it that this spiral wavekin possesses dominion over water, whipping up violent whirlpools and lacerating fishing vessels to shreds...but it is, at least, a very charming little shell.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

The unpredictable patterns on this crustacean's carapace indicate its freshness and depth of flavor when cooked.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

In recent days, dried varieties of this squid have gained popularity as a convenient snack for traveling lancers.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

An elegant jellyfish that emits a warm, gentle glow akin to its namesake.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

Despite being maybe, possibly, improbably the juvenile form of a Ruby Dragon, this wavekin prefers hiding amongst colonies of leopard prawns to confrontation, and is thus the envy of introverted naturalists across the realm.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

With a dorsal fin that makes it look like a standard-bearer, this saltwater fish is ready to charge bravely into a pitched battle under the sea.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A species of shark that is silent but deadly─in the literal sense, children. In the literal sense.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

Though this wavekin may be small, it attempts to remedy such shortcomings by sporting splendidly spectral scales. In doing so, however, it has become more vulnerable to predators and skilled anglers.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A fish of good fortune, said to strongly resemble white and red cords commonly used to wrap gifts in Hingashi.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

This wavekin's golden fins and mouth appear as coins floating in the ocean, giving the impression that sailors of the Kugane coast are quite cavalier with their finances.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Some have spent fortunes to have a single taste of this succulent shrimp.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

If the poisonous sacs of this stingfin are carefully removed, the meat can make for a perfectly adequate meal.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

True to its name, the head of this squid is sharp enough to pierce straight through plate armor.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

A school of these fish creates a striking sheet of silver, like an enormous suit of chainmail drifting through the ocean blue.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Said to be blessed by the gods with blinding speed, sometimes these fish tire of water and propel themselves into the sky on the back of a spectral current.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

The presence of these shellfish in shallow waters is considered to be an ill omen, for they are believed to be the harbinger of storms, violent winds, and worse.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

The fleetness of these sharks is enough to tire even a god, but where divinity sees a menace, a fisher sees opportunity.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

Which came first, the fish or the spade?
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Thought to be the counterpart of the Ruby Dragon, this legendary creature is far less fragile than its name implies.
[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

Found in every corner of the Ruby Sea, this kelp is known and loved for its culinary versatility.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A cephalopod that lays its eggs on the Ruby Sea's rocky reefs.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

If a pinebark flounder splashes in the Ruby Sea and no one is around to hear it, does it make a sound? Far Eastern philosophers have yet to determine a definitive answer.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A moray that resembles an ethereal raiment worn by the Ruby Princess...if ethereal raiments looked as though they were about to utter the punchline to a groan-worthy joke.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

With its fondness for migratory journeys, this saltwater fish puts the “go” in “goby.”
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Said to be an omen of ample harvests, this wavekin is named for a traditional dance passed down in the Far East.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

If one were to liken the spiny lobster to a valiant knight, then the barded lobster─nearly twice the size of its counterpart─would serve as its seaworthy steed.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

As dreadful as it is, people would be forgiven for mistakenly calling this seabeast the “violent sentry.”
[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

Now that its spectral nature has taken precedence, the question of whether this wavekin is a snake or an eel has become irrelevant.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

This shark is believed to be the reincarnation of a tiger descended from Heaven-on-High.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

When winter descends upon Kugane and its vibrant flora wilts, some look to the sea, where the skin of this cephalopod reminds them of warmer seasons.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

The long whiskers of this massive lobster curve like a bow, and some Kugane children cannot resist playing at imaginary war around the dinner table.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Biting into the flesh of this wavekin will stain one's entire mouth black, which is useful if you have occasion to disguise yourself as ancient Far Eastern nobility.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

This wavekin resembles a popular Kugane treat outside of the water, causing sailors to look twice when rummaging through supplies for a late-night snack.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Displaying an almost exclusive predilection for preying on octopodes, this wavekin shows that even nature's deadliest predators can be picky eaters.
[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

The round body of this wavekin allows it to be carried swiftly through the ocean's currents, which might explain why it clings so desperately to the ocean's rocks.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Like its namesake flower, this fish has put many local ecosystems at risk.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

It takes little imagination to guess how this shark, one of two guardians keeping vigil over Shisui of the Violet Tides, got its name.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

What dried flying squid lacks in flavor, it makes up for in sheer quantity, and it is a staple in the diets of the Kugane commonfolk.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

Protected by a thick layer of volcanic rock, this crustacean swims through the depths of the Ruby Sea to keep the flesh inside its shell from cooking.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

If only it knew where to find a pitching carp.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Though this invasive wavekin may appear harmless at first glance, the Yanxians will stop at nothing to hunt these tiny blue terrors down.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

The world may be hard and cold, but this turtle's shell is soft...and questionably warm.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Not deigning to leave her domain, the princess salmon always remains in the waters of the One River.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

When told the tale of this fish's creation, a Doman boy is said to have attempted to create more fish with inky scales. It did not end well for the carp in his father's prized pond.

A small shrimp whose deep green hue is said to be a reflection of the One River. But more importantly, it's delicious.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Beautifully patterned and vibrantly hued, this freshwater fish has long been farmed in the One River for ornamental purposes.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

A large freshwater fish whose eggs are considered so delicious, it gave rise to the saying “hoes before roe”─a reminder that work precedes pleasure.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

The bone-like tongues of these spectral wavekin are surprisingly sturdy despite their crystalline appearance, and are often used by highly skilled artisans to craft priceless accessories.
[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.] [Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

A large shark that, despite its size, prefers living among the reeds of the One River.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

The green carapace of this shrimp is said to be the same emerald hue as the sweeping hills that make up the Gensui Chain.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

This wavekin makes an appearance in the folklore of Yanxia, where it is depicted as a demon who leaves the land fallow. Best eat it to prevent the tales coming true.

Although their early life is spent in Heron's Way, these eels eventually make their way to bigger ponds.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

A bivalve mollusk whose pitch-black shell hides a dazzling interior.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Drawn down the One River from the Azim Steppe, these fish grow fat upon the smaller specimens inhabiting spectral currents.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

The scales of these fish are highly sought after by artisans in Kugane and beyond.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Believed to be a Namazu fallen from grace, this fish can not so much as affirm or deny the claim.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Once the subject of a Far Eastern faerie tale, this wavekin may or may not seek revenge after being used by an adventurous rabbit.

Valued for its vibrant scales, this variety of carp is occasionally mistaken for a gold ingot when viewed from above the water's surface.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Thought to be birthed from the gnarled trunk of an ancient plum tree, the blossoms atop this legendary turtle's shell neither wither nor fade with the passage of time.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]
A set of soft and profoundly healing pillows ideal for relieving back pain.
This apparatus has been guaranteed by science to entertain cats. Whether cats care to entertain the notion of said science, however, is another matter entirely.
A carefully handcrafted replication of a monstrous creature. The longer you stare at it, the longer it stares at you...

Apply directly to the eyeball for optimal exhaustion relief. If you experience side effects such as loss of vision, dizziness, nausea, or death, stop use immediately and seek the counsel of your nearest chirurgeon.
A delightful box brimming with relaxation implements of notable quality.
Simply by holding this miraculous substance in hand, you feel the lingering strain from collecting it fade from your fingers...
But a whiff of this plain material is liable to show any kitty cat a glimpse of kitty heaven.
Everything a monster-lover requires to replicate the horrors of their dreams. Or nightmares, as it were.
Powder that promises to relieve eyestrain once properly prepared. Applying directly to the eyeball is likely to exacerbate ocular discomfort and is highly discouraged.
Relaxation implements of notable quality, sans the delightful box.
This mysteriously sourced gelatin is indeed quite soft to the touch, if fundamentally unnerving in nature...
All you require to create a scientifically certified device for entertaining any cat.
A bag of limbs, eyes, torsos, heads, tails, horns, and claws, mercifully bloodless and in the miniature.
Substances that should create eye drops with a high rate of alleviating ocular stress and a low rate of mortality upon contact.
Materials required to create relaxation implements of notable quality. Delightful box included.
A relic of Aloalo Island surely possessed of immense cultural and anthropological worth.
This esoteric tome discovered on Aloalo Island is a trove of historical knowledge─to those who can decipher it.
Increases EXP earned by 30% when level 90 and below. Attributes and item level vary according to class/job and current level when equipped.
An interior wall delicately stenciled with a cascading leafy design.
For the ambivalent designer who cannot commit to grey or beige. Guaranteed unremarkable!
Simply install this light fixture to be immersed in the magic of the deep. Unsettling fish sold separately by popular request.
An aesthetic arrangement of angling accoutrements.

A sculpture incorporating several of Zeromus's key features, the power to destroy life as we know it thankfully not among them.
※One per estate only.
An elegant fixture reminiscent of Crystarium sensibilities.
Lounge like a highborn tot with this elegant and cozy nursery canopy.
A solid stone hearth rendered in the Ronkan architectural style.
Features a nook beneath the seat for all manner of tomes, dusty or otherwise.
An easily perusable collection of popular periodicals and other publications.
This rounded screen designed to resemble the heavens above is a must-have for astrologians, astrologists, astronomers, and whoever decides to prefix their vocation with “astro” next.
All of the excitement of a true trapdoor, with none of the deadly pits below.

Manderville & Manderville's lovingly crafted Manderville's Adventurer Flakes (Manderville Mark Certified) supplement the diets of growing adventurers with the nutrients they need, while providing the convenience and non-perishability they crave. Now with flavor!

A fraying banner emblazoned with the symbol of the reapers.

A softly glowing lamp of the kind used to provide illumination in the depths of the Aitiascope.
This artifact recovered from the Fell Court of Troia has the distinct air of a furnishing designed for only the greatest of individuals, but technically nothing can stop you from sitting on it.
This whimsical loft was hewn from a centuries-old tree.

This partition features a quaint circular opening certain to invite the sort of guest who is keen on breakfast.
So lifelike is this ornamental moss ball, it looks as though it could up and walk off at any moment, miniature tree and all.

Walk free, and bear the light for others to follow.

A looming reminder of the inexorable march of time.
A trophy that represents the power of teamwork, friendly competition, shared cuisine, hope, dreams, purpose...and batteries.
A masterfully rendered oil depiction of the Allagan atrocities sealed within the Crystal Tower.

A masterfully rendered oil depiction of those who would bring light to the sanctuary of the sylphs.
A masterfully rendered oil depiction of a headstrong woman channeling the Lady of Frost.

A masterfully rendered oil depiction of two brave young women who together traversed myriad memories.
A masterfully rendered oil depiction of Eorzea's many great leaders, united to defend their homeland.
A masterfully rendered oil depiction of a figure blazing her path towards hope.
A heavenly portrait of Byregot, god of architecture and industry.
A heavenly portrait of Rhalgr, god of destruction.
A heavenly portrait of Azeyma, keeper of the sun and goddess of inquiry.
A heavenly portrait of Nald'thal, overseer of the underworld and god of commerce.
A heavenly portrait of Nophica, tender of soils and harvests and goddess of abundance.
A heavenly portrait of Althyk, surveyor of change and space and god of time.
The vibrant flowers of this elegant garden decoration put one in mind of the faeries' colorful homeland. Pixies thankfully not included.
The portability and convenience of this full flight of stairs ultimately render the age-old argument of “ladder versus stepladder” moot.
A charming and romantic pavilion for all those without allergies.
An outdoor lighting fixture of the same ancient Hannish design encountered in the remnants above Alzadaal's Legacy.
A serene decoration fashioned after those thought to exist in ancient times.

A vibrant patch of various wild-growing flora.

A quaint fungal lamp that emits a pale blue glow.

Seeking to make grapes more transportable, a researcher at Meryall Agronomics is rumored to have produced a variety that grew in blocky clusters. Although complaints that they looked unappetizing led to a new strain with rounder edges, the original was regarded fondly by some, and so it was immortalized in the form of this lamppost.

A shallow decorative pool constructed in accordance with Sharlayan sensibilities.

Among sailors, this curious crustacean is jokingly likened to a Roegadyn's girthy fingers.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

These moderately sized wavekin are so eerily pale as to be mistaken for water-bound spirits of the dead.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

These large saltwater fish are known to roam the endless expanse of the Indigo Deep.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

This highly venomous species of anemone is native to the Rhotano Sea.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

These slender wavekin have the dubious honor of being used as writing implements by those at sea bereft of actual pens.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Bright of scale and ferocious in temperament, this large saltwater specimen is a common sight between Thavnair and Eorzea.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

These vicious ancient scalekin have dominated the realm's oceans for millennia.
[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

Allegedly, this many-hued wavekin began its existence as an envoy's attendant who took an unfortunate plunge overboard.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Exposure to spectral currents has endowed the flesh of this rare starfish with crystalline properties.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Given their name by island mammets, these colorful striped wavekin are just as playful as the appellation suggests.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Ignoring their segmented carapace and plethora of other distinguishing features, these substantial crustaceans could, just about, be mistaken for a captain's missing digit.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Bathing in the flows of spectral currents has dyed this coral a startling crimson.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Legends say this vibrantly patterned wavekin was once a royal attendant sadly swallowed up by the waves.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

These glittering wavekin are often mistaken for pouches of ill-gotten gold.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

The observant will note that this slender cylindrical wavekin is roughly the same dimensions as a pen. The insatiably curious will seek to verify whether these poor fish can be used as one.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Comparable to whales in terms of size, this colossal scalekin has endured since ancient times.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

These large saltwater fish are a common sight in the vicinity of the Cieldalaes, their distinctively spiny fins on full display.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

This exceptionally aggressive subspecies of rhotanosaurus is often seen riding spectral currents─its vast shadow inspiring awe and dread in equal measure.
[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

This resplendent red wavekin is no less brilliant than the spectral currents it plies.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Hosting entire ecosystems on their expansive shells, these living islands are the subject of myriad folktales.
[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

These nimble crustaceans are red. Unmistakably, undeniably, resoundingly red.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Prized for their sweet, scrumptious flesh, these crabs must be cooked before consumption, lest one wishes to ingest a bellyful of potent poison.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Some believe these pale, tubular specimens to have once been strands of Saint Agama's stark white hair.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Said to resemble the daggers favored by Thavnairian temple guards, these diminutive wavekin are revered as symbols of good fortune.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

Along with dark clouds on the horizon and the sudden pitter-patter of raindrops, sightings of this species are often interpreted as a sign of impending precipitation.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

This monstrous scalekin has a notably strong skull─one of many evolutionary advantages that include razor-sharp teeth and unparalleled bulk.
[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

Much loved by the local populace, these surprisingly gentle scalekin inhabit the waters around Thavnair.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

This species of grouper is commonly sighted riding spectral currents. The aether it thus absorbs has transformed its flesh into a near-crystalline state.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Revered by inhabitants of fishing villages throughout Thavnair, the distinctive splotches that speckle this graceful wavekin make it easy to spot from a distance.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

These nimble crustaceans are redder than their lesser cousins. Unmistakably, undeniably, resoundingly redder.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

A regular feature of banquets at the satrap's palace, these rare crabs are prized for their exquisite flavor.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Clad in scales so shiny as to be reflective, this wavekin's name means “mirror” in the common tongue.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

The snouts of these aerodynamic wavekin are painfully sharp─so much so that they are occasionally used as darts when dried.
[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

Understood to have persisted in Thavnair since ancient times, this scalekin is currently the subject of feverish Sharlayan scholarship.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

Though its striped carapace evokes a sense of feline ferocity, these mantis shrimp are in actual fact almost hilariously timorous.
[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

There are few creatures known to science that move with the same stubborn lack of urgency as the mehi-mahi.
[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

Of countless species understood to ride spectral currents, this gargantuan scalekin must surely be counted among the largest and most dangerous.
[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

A prominent figure in Thavnairian mythology, this mighty tusked scalekin is said to ward off evil spirits.
[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]
